focus: Energy and commodity trade flows: what has broken in 2026 and where the barrels and cargoes went instead

routes.title: Strait of Hormuz effectively closed
routes.dateRange: Feb 2026–ongoing, still escalating as of Oct 2026
routes.summary: Iran's restriction of traffic through Hormuz — called by the IEA the largest oil-supply disruption in the history of the global oil market — cut ~20% of global oil supply and major LNG volumes. Rather than de-escalating, the crisis has widened through the summer: Iran's newly-formed Persian Gulf Strait Authority blacklisted 45 tankers in August for breaking its transit rules, expanding the list to 56 by early September, and several vessels have since been struck by projectiles or set on fire attempting the crossing. The US Navy is keeping roughly 8 million b/d flowing through naval escort, but ethylene, propylene, benzene and polymer pellets moving through Hormuz still carry elevated war-risk costs, and downstream resin costs remain up to 40% higher in places. Trade press framing: "Hormuz could reopen tomorrow. Resin still wouldn't arrive for 275 days" — the re-contracting and pipeline-fill lag is itself the story. India is the most exposed buyer (60%+ of oil imports from the Middle East, fast-growing resin-consuming packaging sector).

routes.title: Red Sea reopening — Suez traffic recovering
routes.dateRange: Houthi stand-down since Oct 2025 ceasefire; Suez recovery through Oct 2026
routes.summary: The picture has flipped since early 2026: Houthi attacks that shut down the corridor from late 2023 have abated following the October 2025 Israel–Hamas ceasefire, with only scattered incidents since. Suez Canal traffic is recovering sharply — more than 200 ships returned in October 2026 alone, the highest monthly total since the crisis began, with canal revenue up 14% YoY (Jul–Oct). Vessels are gradually peeling back from the Cape of Good Hope detour, recovering the 10–14 transit days it added Asia–Europe. The recovery isn't guaranteed to hold — the Houthis have warned they'll resume attacks if the Gaza ceasefire breaks down — so chemical tankers are only partially unwinding the war-risk premium they'd been carrying through the corridor.

routes.title: Panama Canal — El Niño drought tightens transit limits
routes.summary: What looked like 2023–24-drought recovery has reversed: a severe El Niño (rainfall 34% below average, May–Aug) forced the Canal Authority to impose its first daily transit cap since the 2023–24 crisis — cut to 34 ships/day on Sep 3, then 32 from Sep 15, versus a normal ~36 — alongside progressive draft cuts at the Neopanamax locks, down to 47.5 ft by Oct 1. VLGC/LPG freight rates have hit record highs as US Gulf Coast propane and propylene shipments compete for scarce slots, directly squeezing the Houston-to-Asia petrochemical export route this entry tracks. Some easing is scheduled — Neopanamax daily transits rise from 9 to 10 (33 total daily slots) from Oct 15 — but capacity stays well below normal.

routes.title: Petrochemicals: China flips from PE/PP importer to exporter
routes.dateRange: April 2026 export surge; durability debated through Oct 2026
routes.summary: China's PE/PP imports hit record lows in April 2026 while its own PE exports hit record highs (+122% YoY; +479% YoY in April alone). This structurally squeezes the market US Gulf Coast exporters were counting on, landing right as ~3.3 million tonnes/year of new US PE capacity (Shell, Baystar, Nova, Dow) has come online since 2023 — a demand-side story compounding the transport-side disruptions above. How durable it is remains an open question: Argus flags the surge as possibly reflecting domestic oversupply and weak demand rather than a lasting trade-flow reversal, and October data show China's PP trade still net-import, with both import and export legs cooling month-on-month.

routes.title: US Gulf Coast new PE capacity chasing a shrinking export pool
routes.summary: ~2 million tonnes/year of new HDPE capacity — Golden Triangle Polymers, the Chevron Phillips Chemical–QatarEnergy joint venture — starting up in Orange, TX in H2 2026 alone, almost entirely aimed at export, on top of 3.3M+ tonnes/year added since 2023 (Shell, Baystar, Nova, Dow) — landing in the same export markets China has just started competing for directly.
